audio_caption: The audio clip begins with an excited male voice stating "this spot has definitely not been worked before, it's not finding way more gold than I thought I would be finding." This is followed by energetic bluegrass music featuring banjo and acoustic instruments, creating an upbeat and adventurous mood. A male voice then greets listeners with "Good morning or good afternoon," stating that they will be "sniping" at a location they haven't visited in a while. The music continues in the background while the speaker talks about expectations of finding gold. The male voice adds, with a light tone, "This tickles". A new male voice describes the area as "a beautiful place" and exclaims "look at that leaf, how majestic," before making a splashing sound.

The clip begins with a male speaker introducing the tools for the day, including pokey sticks and a snuffer bottle, and mentioning a GoPro to film the adventures. He announces they're ready and switching to GoPro. The audio cuts to a crash, followed by the speaker stating he accidentally took Emily Riddell's left boot and that his left boot is still normal Alaska. Next, laughter is heard, then an underwater sound effect. The speaker discusses the pros and cons of sniping in the summertime, mentioning the water being low but also silty and dirty. After this, he announces that they got their first piece of gold, adding that the GoPro is shooting in wide and so things might look smaller than usual. Underwater sounds reappear.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker expressing his fortune at discovering gold, particularly at his first location. The background features consistent, rhythmic sounds suggesting underwater activity, possibly related to diving or exploration. The speaker sounds excited. A distinct scraping sound interrupts the underwater ambience, followed by the speaker noting that the GoPro camera colors make it difficult to see, but he claims there is gold. The sound of scraping returns. The speaker notes that the spot provides gold year after year. The speaker says there must be “15 little pieces”. The speaker concludes by stating that intersections of cracks hold the most gold, especially as you go down. This fades into upbeat electronic music.

The audio begins with a male speaker soliciting requests for more underwater gold videos, encouraging viewers to engage with the channel in an enthusiastic tone. He then transitions to describing the "hardpack," which is gravel sitting for so long that it hardens. Bubbling sounds and the movement of water under the river indicate underwater activity. After which, the male speaker excitedly announces a new find, describing its movement and composition. The clip ends with advice on removing lead from the river and underwater noise.

A male voice begins, speaking calmly about patience when working with clay underwater, stating there will be times where “you're just going to wait, at least four decades until the smoke clears.” Sounds of rushing water, bubbling, and liquid are audible underneath the speech. A different male voice breaks in, speaking in a practical tone about clearing “overburden in the area” to make room for “crevicing because there’s just too much material that’s falling down into the crevice.” The first speaker returns, excited, announcing finding “a little piece of gold." The sound of rushing water intensifies, along with an odd, resonant humming. The first speaker notes “That’s a nice-looking crevice.” before the second speaker remarks that “This spot has definitely not been worked before,” explaining that he’s “finding way more gold than I thought I would be finding.” The first speaker closes, observing, despite the small size, it is “super addictive to find gold in nature like this.” The sounds of rushing water and bubbling continue throughout.

The clip begins with a male speaker enthusiastically recommending underwater gold hunting. He asks, "How you doing?" in a friendly tone. After a brief pause, another male voice says, "Ruining things, moving things." The first speaker elaborates, noting that he had to open his wetsuit to cool off because it's warm, especially the thick wetsuit he's wearing. He explains the climate of Vancouver Island, suggesting that viewers get an 8-millimeter semi-dry wetsuit if they want to get into sniping. He gives a shout-out to Wilson's Diving in Victoria, BC. Then, music starts, a rock-style track with electric guitar and drums, creating an adventurous and edgy tone. The speaker returns, predicting a couple of pieces of gold under a rock. He comments on a "wild cody croc" waiting to snap for gold. As the music continues, there's underwater bubbling, indicating that someone is swimming. The male voice repeats, "Just keep swimming, swimming, swimming."

The clip begins with a male speaker, sounding excited, saying he "found this thin crack here," and after clearing rocks, "found one little piece of candy." Following that is a short music interlude, reminiscent of an upbeat, almost chiptune-like video game theme. A new male voice, also excited, announces he just "spotted a piece of gold," and then exclaims "oh, a piece of candy," followed by an "ooh" sound and heavy breathing. The music returns, this time, more suspenseful in tone. The male voice continues, saying "it went up the snuffer, so it wasn't that big." It fades out with the music continuing.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker instructing someone, likely a dog, to start with "three pieces at the bottom of this little crevice," encouraging it to look up. The sounds of what seems to be a dog panting and sniffing are evident, suggesting the dog is actively engaged in something. The speaker follows this up with an exclamation, "look guys stuck." Another male speaker says, "way to go!" Lastly, the music starts, featuring a bluesy electric guitar and slow, dark melody.

The audio clip starts with the sound of water flowing gently, suggesting a natural setting, followed by a male speaker who seems tired, saying it's "hard to stop, especially when you keep finding more gold." The ambient sounds of the water continue. A distinct slurping sound occurs. A male voice shouts "Yay!" indicating excitement. The speaker then reflects they had been "messing around for just a little bit longer" and it's "it for Poly." A sound, possibly from an action, transitions the speaker to saying it's "it for me." The speaker is "already exhausted" but thought the group "did really well." Music starts quietly in the background with a reflective mood.

The clip begins with sounds of water, likely from the ocean or a large body of water. A male speaker is heard saying "I'm gonna get out of my wetsuit" followed by "and I'll take a look at the gold that we found." The speaker's tone suggests excitement or anticipation. This is followed by a brief sound that might be a gasp, possibly from exertion.

The clip begins with an outdoor environment characterized by the sound of water. A male speaker, sounding pleased and speaking in an excited tone, mentions being out of his wetsuit and how the day is better because he found more gold than expected. He mentions checking out "Cody's pan" and notes his "signature is on there," observing that it's "not too bad." He expresses fondness for the yellow and shiny gold. Another man speaks, indicating it is enough to "keep me going." The initial male speaker transitions to discussing the "little pan" and emphasizing "how you use it." The sound of water persists as the clip concludes.

The audio begins with speech, a man speaking in a casual tone, noting he has "lead pellets in there," and then describes "beautiful yellow candy," speculating on its weight in ounces and grams. His intonation suggests he's unsure. The audio ends abruptly.

The clip opens with a single male speaker, happy and excited about his gold find, mentioning it being "all dried up", not looking "too bad", and really liking the spot. He's disappointed about not finding "big nuggets" but hopes for the next time. Next, he indicates he will put it on "the scale" before the clip transitions to the sound of rocks clattering, followed by the man stating "45 ounces" and "on the nose" with surprise. Then he reiterates the measurement, this time in grams, stating it's "very rare you get a solid number", followed by him stating "cool".

The audio clip begins with a male speaker discussing gold, noting that "two grams of gold isn't bad". He mentions that in dollar form, it's around "$120-ish dollars", and he's not doing this "for the gold value". However, he has found over $1000 worth of gold in a day before. He speaks in a conversational and informative tone. He ends by saying, "Anyways, that is it for this video".

The clip begins with a male speaker encouraging viewers to subscribe if they enjoyed the content and to follow his adventures. He then mentions his presence on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and Patreon for exclusive content. He expresses gratitude to his viewers for their support and signs off. This is followed by a black screen with a logo.
